contents: Equipment-reported yield and full-inspection good yield did not agree, so true process defects and inspection misclassification had to be separated under one basis. I aligned the yield denominator and measurement criteria, then managed owners, deadlines, local 4M+2E retests, and decision criteria on the same cells. I contributed to the team result of stabilizing monthly average good yield from about 40% to 98.7% and directly revised the MSA criteria, SOP, QCP, P-FMEA, and inspection standards.

title: 2170 Assembly-Line Good-Yield Stabilization

contents: No equipment could run automatically from Start through completion and normal MES history was absent, so assembly production-start conditions had to be rechecked against an initial SAT baseline. I set assembly-wide trial and acceptance criteria and managed local 4M+2E, punch owners, deadlines, and retests. Two 100-cell lots and a final 50-cell one-way run confirmed the limited-production start conditions, and I revised or created work standards, QCP, P-FMEA, checklists, and MES control items.

contents: Electrolyte, clad tab, turn count, can height, and inspection conditions all changed from the existing 2170 cell, requiring new process conditions from impregnation through downstream assembly. I translated CTQs and changes into local 4M+2E trials and managed sample builds, inspection, evaluation, gates, and control documents from project kickoff. A/B/C samples, about 20,000-cell trial production, customer qualification, and CCB P.O approval were completed; commercial production did not proceed because of pricing.

contents: With no dedicated equipment or jigs, the existing 4695 line had to produce a tabless structure while internal laser entry, shorts, and assembly damage were checked. I set process conditions and temporary 3D-printed jigs, then directly built samples and performed laser welding, assembly, sectioning, teardown, Hi-Pot, and functional evaluation. Failure modes were separated across about 100 exploratory builds, producing five functional samples and confirming A-sample structural build feasibility and functional direction.

contents: Limited FAT samples and individual auto cycles could not prove end-to-end flow, repeatability, or readiness for actual production. I built acceptance sheets and punch lists, tracked supplier corrections and retests, and led actual cell production plus measurement and process-standard work. The team observed an initial snapshot of about 95% over roughly five days and 1,000 cells, including cells meeting criteria after rework, and documented FAT/SAT, MSA, and operating standards. It is not FPY or long-term production yield.

contents: One incumbent can supplier could not cover planned volume alone, and alloy, thickness, tolerance, and burr differences had to be checked for assembly, sealing, and safety impact. I owned change and incoming review, beading/crimping/sizing/laser conditions, sample builds, sectioning, teardown, safety and performance tests, and control documents. Three lots of 200 cells and official UN38.3 passed, and follow-on pilot production plus purchase orders moved to the alternative can in March 2025.

title: Alternative Can Supplier 600-Cell / 3-Lot Pilot Transition Validation

contents: Manual shaping before pre-welding varied by operator and repeatedly created uncoated-edge damage and short-circuit risk. I separated the positive- and negative-electrode damage mechanisms, built a temporary jig, defined shape, position, and acceptance criteria, and ran sample and teardown tests. The condition was verified with about 400 samples, used in subsequent pilot production, and reflected in process/inspection standards, the P-FMEA, and production-equipment RFQ.

contents: Process-level MES data existed, but a cell's full history was not connected, so investigating ten customer-requested cells took about three days. After a MES enhancement request was rejected for cost, I spent about three weeks building Power Query consolidation and Excel VBA search and linking logic. A single search took 5–10 seconds and a ten-cell investigation about three minutes; the tool was used on site during my employment and handed over.

contents: At YMC's new-business start, the new model had no parts list, overhaul manuals, inspection manual, or precision-setting criteria. I performed the full incoming-to-teaching flow and created manuals and training for disassembly, replacement, precision assembly, alignment, zero, leak, FARO checks, and teaching. Initial YMC qualification and about five units of one model were followed by deeper repeat-overhaul, operator, parts, and field standards at Bontech.

contents: A higher OLED process temperature exposed cracks and particles in a mixed-acid film for upper-electrode-type parts, while susceptor-type parts required a separate high-temperature qualification. Using a Six Sigma GB problem-solving sequence, I produced and evaluated samples, separated causes with 4M+2E, ran scale-up tests, and documented process and inspection criteria. The mixed-acid condition passed customer qualification and received about one year of additional follow-up; the oxalic-acid condition completed repeated 450℃ screening and customer vacuum-heat qualification before about one year of use.

contents: Legacy bath values appeared normal, but etch-rate, particle, and film-quality problems repeated after about three months. I increased sampling to twice weekly and connected component-level analysis, external comparisons, and batch-test sample evaluation for Korea and China. The project standardized the analysis SOP, log sheet, replenishment/replacement decision, and product-sample checks for the target baths and China site.

contents: Counterpart samples from the same bath and process still produced different Hi-Pot decisions when equipment, repeats, and test sequence differed. I led the English specification, process and run-sheet work, sample production and measurement, external analysis, technical audit, and corrective retest closure. One audit finding was closed through aligned measurement conditions and retesting, followed by qualification notice and about one year of supply.

contents: The initial chemical-plus-ultrasound trial reduced stripping time, but removing the chemical without fume exhaust increased work time, manual effort, and surface damage. I ran lab and full-part trials, roughness, microscopy and SEM–EDS analysis, and documented overlap, relative-motion, and reusability risks. Normal operation stopped because cavitation erosion, particles, and reuse failed; the case produced stop gates for future scale-up.

title: Diffuser Ultrasonic Stripping Scale-up Failure and Stop Gates

contents: A model trained on public weld images lost substantial performance on practical specimens containing soot, spatter, reflections, and capture variation. I planned the overall project, compared candidate models and error images using recall and FPR, and owned low-resolution coordinate scaling and threshold FN/FP decisions. Recall on captured specimens rose from 15.84% to 85.15%, a gain of 69.31 percentage points, and the team completed a ResNet+DeiT and FastAPI/PWA inspection demo.

title: Building an AI Model to Find Defects in Welding Images

contents: Physical-equipment try-out requires repeated material and engineering effort, while inconsistent state meaning across PLC, equipment, and monitoring makes chronic loss difficult to trace. The ten-person team demonstrated Factory I/O, PLC/Ladder, SCADA/OPC UA, and web integration. DQN remained a model-selection and integration-design layer.

contents: Manufacturing, semiconductor, and battery knowledge accumulated with inconsistent terms and links, making evidence retrieval difficult. I structured the Markdown/YAML vault and link-graph index, then built a CLI that synchronizes changed files to ChromaDB and retrieves/reranks candidates. Markdown source management, incremental synchronization, candidate retrieval, and reranking are implemented. Source-location display, authorization, and repeated retrieval evaluation can extend it into an operating manufacturing-knowledge tool.

I linked questions, theory, sources, rights, and publication state and implemented learner flow and publication rules that prevent pre-submission answer exposure. The masterbook publishes only supported items and keeps conflicting or rights-uncertain material on HOLD.
